newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA Curacao refinery sees higher throughput. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PDVSA Curacao refinery sees higher throughput. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: The fire-hit oil refinery in Curacao, operated by Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), could reach 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude throughput within 1-2 weeks from 105,000 bpd processing at the moment, an official at the plant said on Friday.
The refinery was hit by a serious fire on Thursday (corrects from Friday) morning, which cut throughput by 130,000 bpd to 60,000 bpd.
PDVSA's Punta Cardon refinery in mainland Venezuela has increased throughput by about 30,000 bpd to compensate for some of the lost Curacao processing, the official added.
On Friday morning, Curacao was running at 105,000 bpd using crude unit number two for 60,000 bpd and the rest in a thermal cracking unit converted to distill crude.

Following an initial visual inspection, the official said the fire damage at crude unit number three was less serious than first thought, and the worst effects were concentrated in the vacuum section of the unit.

"The main damage was in the vacuum tower so there is a possibility that we take the atmospheric tower into operation earlier... I would say in one or two weeks. In that case we would only be 10,000 bpd below normal throughput," he said.
The atmospheric tower can run 120,000 bpd of crude oil.

He said 50,000 bpd of Lagomar crude, used to make lubricants, that was scheduled to be processed in the Curacao plant would now be processed in the Cardon refinery and Cardon had increased throughput to about 305,000 bpd from 275,000 bpd.
"We are going to get the long residue from the Cardon refinery. They will process the Lagomar crude and then send us the residue used for our paraffinic lube oil train," the official said.
He said if throughput was restored in Curacao's burned crude unit, then unit number two would be taken out of operation for maintenance, which had been planned for this week.
